agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The sink write of L25h2 suppresses special and HTML end tokens: id 1 (EOS, z −17.3), "", "", "", an unused token, and "" (z −9.2). That is typical last-layer bookkeeping: a constant "don't end yet" bias that other components override once an answer is complete. Still, the model gets cut at the token limit in 23% of answers. A too-strong stop suppression would show up as answers that state their final answer and then fail to emit "". I will count how many cut answers already contain a final-answer statement ("Final Answer", "####", "\boxed"), and for those, look at what follows it and whether the gold answer was given there. If many cut answers ran past a correct final answer, this head is a stopping-failure mechanism worth repairing. If cut answers rarely contain a final statement, the loops come from reasoning, as seen so far.

None of the 124 cut answers contains a final-answer statement. The loops happen in the middle of the reasoning, so the end-of-turn suppression by L25h2 is ordinary bookkeeping, not a stopping failure. That line is closed too.

Before deciding whether anything is left to repair, I want to revisit one structural oddity I dismissed earlier. In layers 4 and 6–10, post_attention_layernorm has 41–64 dimensions with scale |1+w| < 0.1, while the median scale there is 1–10. Attention is therefore all but barred from writing those coordinates.

If those were set by hand, which would be a capacity limiter on information flow, the values would sit exactly at zero (w = −1 in bf16). Natural training would give small but scattered nonzero values. I will count exact zeros versus near zeros in every norm vector, and look at how the near-zero values are distributed.

Exact zeros concentrated in these layers would be a planted mask to test by restoring it. Scattered small nonzero values would be natural and close the norm line for good.

The last scan found no planted mask in the norms. post_attention_layernorm has only 0–6 exact zeros per layer, and its near-zero scales are scattered small values (quartiles 0.016–0.039). pre_feedforward_layernorm has 1–2 exact zeros per layer, a consistent pattern that most likely reflects Gemma's massive-activation dimensions. So the norm line is closed.
